title: StyroStone: A protocol for scanning and extracting three-dimensional meshes of stone artefacts using Micro-CT scanners
author: Dominik Göldner
materials: Cover the Styrofoam faces with Styrofoam slabs.
Generate isosurface again for cropped scan.
Do not change pre-selected file type (.hx).
Crop the lines to separate them.
Select ‘Lasso selection’ in the Eraser Panel.
Move the separated lines into their respective folder.
Crop the stone artefacts to separate them.
Artec Studio will automatically run the ‘Fine registration’.
Removing the base and outlying material.
Navigate to and select the target folder.

steps.title: Prepare Styrofoam Body
steps.instruction: Create a Styrofoam holder for the artefacts based on the micro-CT scanner's size limitations.

substeps.instruction: Cut a Styrofoam rectangle (e.g., 25 cm height x 22 cm width x 5 cm thickness).
Optional: Glue an additional Styrofoam support base (ca. 2 cm height, slightly wider than the contact area) using Polyvinyl acetate (white glue).
Draw guiding/separation lines with a dark marker on both sides (Face A and Face B) to determine rows.
Mark Face A with a dot or 'A' for identification.

steps.title: Insert and Document Artefacts
steps.instruction: Secure the artefacts into the Styrofoam and record their exact positions.

substeps.instruction: Carve holes roughly the dimensions of the artefacts using a box cutter.
Insert artefacts into holes, starting from the leftmost position of the first row on Face A, moving right, then down to the next row. Repeat for Face B.
Ensure consistent orientation: dorsal face upwards, proximal side at the bottom, and longest axis vertical.
Immediately document the position of each artefact in a spreadsheet (e.g., MS Excel) using a code (e.g., S1-FA-L2.5 for Styrofoam 1, Face A, Line 2, position 5).
Take reference pictures of both faces, including a close-up of the first artefact in the first row of each face.

steps.title: Seal Styrofoam Body
steps.instruction: Secure the artefacts within the body for scanning.

substeps.instruction: Cover Face A and B with thin Styrofoam slabs (ca. 1 cm thickness) of the same dimensions as the main body.
Tightly secure the slabs and main body with plastic rubber bands (do not glue).
Label each Styrofoam body with a number.

steps.title: Perform Micro-CT Scanning
steps.instruction: Scan the prepared Styrofoam body using a micro-CT scanner.

substeps.instruction: Place the Styrofoam body on the scanner's turning base and secure it with strong double-sided tape.
Position the turning base as far from the source as possible to increase the field of view (note: this decreases resolution).
Set scanning parameters; for multiple specimens, use the 'multiscans' option to scan layers by Styrofoam height.
Ensure layer borderlines do not intersect stone tools to avoid 'merging lines' artefacts.
Use a resolution of ca. 140 microns (or as appropriate for the material).
Save scans and metadata (e.g., .pcr file) including voxel size, volume dimensions (x, y, z), and image data type (e.g., 16 bit).

steps.title: Post-Scan Recovery
steps.instruction: Retrieve the artefacts from the scanner.

substeps.instruction: Remove the Styrofoam body from the scanner.
Remove rubber bands and covering plates.
Remove artefacts one by one and return them to their find bags.

steps.title: Import and Configure Data in Avizo Lite
steps.instruction: Load the CT scan and apply metadata for correct scaling.

substeps.instruction: Open Avizo and load the .vol file.
In 'File Format Selection', choose 'Raw Data'.
In 'Out-of-Core Data', select 'Read complete volume into memory'.
In 'Raw Data Parameters', set 'Data type' (usually '16-bit unsigned').
Open the .pcr metadata file in Notepad to find ROI_SizeX, ROI_SizeY, and ROI_SizeZ (or Volume_Size) and VoxelSizeRec.
Enter these dimensions and voxel size into the 'Raw Data Parameters' window (Header value should change to 0 if correct).
Set the unit in the 'Units Editor' based on the metadata file.

steps.title: Generate and Refine Isosurface
steps.instruction: Create a 3D surface that separates artefacts from the Styrofoam.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Isosurface' button to generate a scan isosurface.
Adjust the 'Threshold' value to separate artefacts from air/Styrofoam.
Use 'Down Sample' for fast testing of threshold values; repeat until a good separation is achieved.
Once a threshold is found, disable 'Down Sample' and apply the threshold again for the final model.
Inspect the model for noise or surface inconstancies.

steps.title: Crop and Extract Surface in Avizo
steps.instruction: Isolate the artefacts from the surrounding material and export the mesh.

substeps.instruction: Switch to orthographic view using the 'Eye' sign.
Rotate the model and use the 'Cropping tool' (Cursor sign -> first Tool sign) to narrow the bounding box around the artefacts.
Apply changes to delete excluded materials.
Generate a new 'Isosurface' on the cropped volume using the previously identified threshold (with 'Down Sample' disabled).
Select the resulting isosurface and click 'Extract Surface'.
Apply the 'Extract Surface' menu parameters and click 'Apply'.
Export the 'ExtractedSurface' label via 'File' -> 'Export data as' to the target folder.
Save the Avizo project using 'Minimize project size' policy.

steps.title: Separate Faces in Artec Studio
steps.instruction: Split the combined 3D model into individual faces (A and B).

substeps.instruction: Copy the extracted model file twice (one for Face A, one for Face B, one backup).
Import the model into Artec Studio and switch to orthographic view (NUM 5).
Rotate the model so faces are parallel.
Use 'Editor' -> 'Eraser' -> 'Lasso selection' (Ctrl + left click) to select and delete Face B to isolate Face A.
Use the Lasso tool again to delete any remaining outlying materials.
Export the cleaned face as a mesh (.ply, .stl, .obj, or .wrl) and save as 'Styro [X]_Face [A/B]_Cropped and Cleaned'.
Repeat the process for Face B using the second copy of the model.

steps.title: Separate Lines in Artec Studio
steps.instruction: Isolate individual rows of artefacts from each face.

substeps.instruction: Open the cleaned face model in Artec Studio.
Rotate the model so the first artefact is at the upper left, matching the reference list and pictures.
Use 'Editor' -> 'Eraser' -> 'Lasso selection' (Ctrl + left click) to select and delete all rows except the one being isolated (or select the target row and use 'Inverse').
Export the separated line (e.g., 'Styro 1_Line 1').
Use Ctrl+Z or 'Edit' -> 'Undo' to recall the deleted lines.
Repeat for all lines in the face.

steps.title: Isolate Individual Artefacts
steps.instruction: Extract each stone artefact from its respective line.

substeps.instruction: Open a separated line model in Artec Studio.
Rotate the model to ensure the first artefact is in the upper left.
Use 'Editor' -> 'Eraser' -> 'Lasso selection' (Ctrl + left click) to select and delete all artefacts except the target one (or use 'Inverse').
Export the isolated artefact using the actual artefact ID and optional location ID (e.g., S1-FA-L1.1_10401).
Export in required formats (e.g., .ply, .stl), specifically including .wrl for AGMT-3D.
Use Ctrl+Z or 'Edit' -> 'Undo' to recall deleted artefacts and repeat for all specimens in the line.

steps.title: Perform Virtual Control Measurements
steps.instruction: Verify the accuracy of the 3D models using MeshLab.

substeps.instruction: Load the artefact model into MeshLab and switch to orthographic view (Press 5).
Select the 'Point to Point Measure Tool'.
Click the starting and end points of a linear measurement (e.g., maximum length).
If rotation is needed, press 'Esc' to leave the tool, rotate, and press 'Esc' again to return.
Compare the virtual measurement in the Log Panel with physical database measurements.

steps.title: Scan Larger Artefacts with Artec Scanner
steps.instruction: Use a handheld Artec scanner for larger objects that cannot fit in the micro-CT setup.

substeps.instruction: Calibrate the Artec scanner according to the manual.
Set up a white turntable (optionally marked with random red and blue circles).
Secure the artefact vertically on the turntable using modeling clay.
Start pre-scanning (button up on handle) and adjust distance until the object appears green on screen.
Start scanning (button up) and slowly spin the turntable while monitoring the screen.
Stop scanning (button down) and repeat the process for the opposite side of the artefact.
In Artec Studio 'Editor' -> 'Eraser', align the model so the base is horizontal and delete the base/clay using the Lasso tool (Ctrl + left click).
Use 'Align' -> 'Auto-alignment' (or manual alignment using 3-5 homologous point pairs) to merge sub-scans.
Apply 'Global registration' (default: Geometry and texture, Key frame ratio 0.1, Search features 50mm).
Apply 'Sharp fusion' (default: 3D resolution 1mm, Hole radius max 5mm).
Apply 'Hole filling' (default: Hole perimeter max 100mm).
Apply 'Small-object filter' (Remove surfaces: All except largest).
Save the project and export the final ply mesh.

steps.title: Export Non-Binary PLY for geomorph
steps.instruction: Convert models to non-binary PLY format for use in the R package geomorph.

substeps.instruction: Load the artefact model into MeshLab.
Switch to orthographic view (Press 5).
Export the mesh via 'File' -> 'Export Mesh As...' (or Ctrl+Shift+E).
In the 'Choose Saving Options' panel, disable 'Binary encoding'.
Save the file.
